2025 · Developer tools·CMS

Installations Page

Designed and shipped installation analytics that gave developers site-level visibility into how their apps were used

TL;DR

The problemI designed a page that developers needed: they had no way to see who installed their apps, so they emailed support for basic usage data.

ProcessI mapped the gap with the PM, worked through permission levels and PII limits with engineering, and shipped part of it in code.

The resultDevelopers who found it used it, and the feedback has been positive.

The problemDevelopers couldn't see who installed their apps

Developers built workarounds and emailed our team just to get basic user data.

It came up in almost every developer interview.

“On every install, I create an instance in my database, including the email of the site owner…”App developer
“If we could get more info about WIX users, like Shopify partners dashboard, that would be great…”Customer support manager

The problems it caused

No way to support their users

No way to email or upsell to them

Basic feature that the competitors had

Emails to our support team for basic data

ApproachMost of the work was scoping the table

I worked with several teams to organize the data we wanted to show developers.

App Developers. What they needed to know about their users

Account managers. What content requests they get from app developers

Our developers. What data the server holds

Legal. What we are allowed to show about users

Competitors. Shopify and App Store Connect

Design principles

Four principles came out of the research and the constraints.

01

Explain, don't hide

When data is restricted or missing, a tooltip says why and how to get access.

Clarity
02

Start from what developers asked for

The default view comes from the interviews and requests.

Relevance
03

Legal sets the boundaries

PII and legal rules decided what could be shown, and to whom, before any layout.

Compliance
04

Let developers shape the view

Filters, column customization, and export.

Flexibility

ExplorationCreated a quick mock to test the direction

  • Figma Make. A working mock with data built before detailed design. This helped me see how to distribute data and set the default view.
  • Validated With stakeholders and users before investing in the final layout.

SolutionA default view developers can customize

  • Default columns. Built from the interviews: business name, site URL, email, plan, version, install date and rating.
  • Download csv. This was also highly requested for developers to use in their own database or export filtered users.

Customize the viewColumns and filters

  • Always shown. Business name and site URL.
  • Developers choose the rest. Instance ID, email, version and install date are on by default.
  • Finding specific users.

Missing dataExplaining missing data

  • Empty cells. Developers should know why information is missing, so cells and columns have tooltips that give the reason, for example a review made in the Standalone App Market. I mapped every empty state to a reason, with the server team.
  • Empty state. Shown when a developer has no installations.

Behind the scenes

Edge & empty states

Delivery & challengesWorking with the team

Process

My partners. The PM, developers including the backend developer who owned the data, Legal and a content writer.

PRD and scoping. I worked on planning the product.

Joined the development team. I used Cursor and Claude Code to add features and fix bugs.

Documentation writing. I led it and drafted the documentation with the technical writers.

A design system contribution. A year selector, built in code and now available across the platform.

Saved views. I shipped them myself, in code.

Challenges

Incorrect data. The server returned wrong data, and I caught it during QA.

Product handoffs. Each time the product owner changed, I kept the context.

A complex migration. We launched with a small controlled rollout. It is live now.

Export function was harder than expected. It rolled out later than the rest.

Legal and permissions. Personal emails need a permission and user consent.

Results & ImpactDevelopers adopted the top requested page

Developers got a page per app with filters, column customization, saved views and export, so they no longer need to keep their own installation records.

"We already had email sequences hooked on webhooks, but this lets us manually follow up with users - especially for the non-technical team members."
"Very good feature overall - thank you!"

Discovery

Since opening to all developers, the majority of those who visited the WixWix is a website builder and development platform used by millions of businesses and creators worldwide. Developer Center and had published apps discovered the page, through a "New" badge.

Actions

Of those who saw it, the majority took action: copying data, opening sites and applying filters.

No promotion

All of this after a quiet launch.

Next steps

Contacts, an account view and cancellation reasons.
